notes: §1985:XIII.4.9.4 GR2: "Within a declarative procedure, there must be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures." Every procedure-name reference (PERFORM, PERFORM THRU, GO TO, GO TO DEPENDING, ALTER) passes ProcedureTableBuilder.ResolveProcedureOperand, which calls StatementValidation.CheckDeclarativesBoundary: a reference written in a declarative section that names a nondeclarative procedure draws warning COBOL2375 at every edition (a general rule on the program; the warning severity is the docs/CONFORMANCE.md 'Declaratives reference boundary' determination), and the 2023 RESUME exemption cannot reach 85 because RESUME is refused there (COBOL0876). Probes at 85 (work-slice-54/c1*; classes b, c, f): PERFORM, PERFORM THRU (both ends), GO TO, GO TO DEPENDING (value 0 falls through), ALTER ... TO PROCEED TO and PERFORM of a nondeclarative section each print COBOL2375 at the statement; RESUME NEXT STATEMENT prints COBOL0876; the witness's PERFORM and GO TO of paragraphs of its own declarative section run with no diagnostic.

next.reason: 1985: "Within a declarative procedure, there must be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures."; 2023: "there shall be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures except in a RESUME statement.". The same prohibition is kept, but 2023 adds an exception: a RESUME statement in a declarative may reference a nondeclarative procedure, which 1985 refused.
